best_parts: node skin_t12 / case_t1: 'That choice is not right' then a tempting-reason sentence, then a refutation, plus a sure_note that names the belief (FNAC as the key exams repeat)
node lobular: a short explain that links ILC bilaterality to MRI extent and high-risk screening, giving O2 a home on the path
node nipple_t20 / nipple_reveal: separates 'most common' from 'must exclude' and offers Show me why after the hint
flaws: node case: the 45-year-old lump 'core or FNAC' stem replays the S1 test-for-a-lump probe, so the retest is the same form, not a new one (R2)
node case_imaging: the 27-year-old imaging stem replays the S1 TR17 probe; the two trap options both point to img_t17, so the second one is a near-duplicate of the first
node final: the stem 'Planning needs invasion and receptor status' names the answer before the learner chooses, so the key is findable by reading the stem (DP1)
node skin: the 3 cm peau d'orange stem repeats the S2 TR12 probe nearly verbatim

best_parts: node lump_t1: the classmate framing makes the old key feel like a peer's advice, so the trap is tempting; the feedback names why and refutes it
node tcat: the T3 size partial and the T4d trap sit beside the key, so the learner must choose between skin and size, not just the sign
node staging_p: the MRI partial is a real neighbour of the correct 'no scan' answer, so surface knowledge does not settle it
flaws: path: no node teaches invasive lobular carcinoma or the BRCA mapping on this path, although O2 is an S3 objective. O2 is tagged only on node nip, which teaches bloody discharge (R3)
node lump / triple: the 45-year-old lump 'core or FNAC' stem is asked twice here and replays the S1 probe, so the segment's first two probes repeat S1 (R2)
node img: the 27-year-old imaging stem replays the S1 TR17 probe
nodes triple_t5, lump_p, img_t17: wrong-option feedback offers only 'Try again', with no hint or Show me why, so a second miss gets no second explanation (R5)

best_parts: node imaging: the 28-year-old and 52-year-old contrast in one stem is a new form of TR17, not a replay of S1, and it makes the learner set age against test
node mri: a short explain that connects MRI's role to lobular extent and high-risk screening, so O2 is taught on the path
node nipple: predict-first probe, Show me why on the hint, and a sure_note that splits 'commonest' from 'must exclude'
flaws: node skin: the 3 cm peau d'orange stem repeats the S2 TR12 probe, and the probe has no size partial (T3), so only one trap is offered
node tissue: the neoadjuvant core-versus-FNAC stem repeats the S1 TR1 concept, so the retest is again the same form
node nipple: the only trap is 'Carcinoma breast' and there is no partial, so the probe is easier than the other S3 probes

c's mri explain node with a's lobular explain wording, so O2 is taught on every path
